newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Inflation fears to discourage Portugal rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Inflation fears to discourage Portugal rate cut.

text.p: The Bank of Portugal was expected to leave its key rates unchanged on Tuesday because of lingering concern over inflation and the recent weakness of the escudo, analysts said.
All nine analysts polled by Reuters said they believed the central bank would not alter rates on Tuesday when it announces conditions for the next commercial bank reserve period at 1415 GMT.
The repo rate stands at 6.50 percent, while the Bank's so-called drain rate -- used to absorb market funds -- is 6.20 percent.

"Rate cuts will depend on the forex and fixed income markets. If spreads of Portuguese bonds against Bonos narrow again, the Bank of Portugal could cut rates before April," said Cristina Casalinho of Banco Portugues de Investimento.
The Bank of Portugal said last week that inflation will fall more quickly from April. "The trend of disinflation will be more noticeable from April," it said.

An analyst with a national bank who asked not to be identified said: "At the European level there is no climate of lowering rates. There were times in the past when the market clearly anticipated rate cuts and the Bank of Portugal was not far behind."
"But today there is some caution. The market is not pressuring the Bank of Portugal so much (to cut)," he added.
Jorge Ferraz of IMF-Informacao de Mercados Financeiros believes that there is no urgency for the central bank to act.
"The Bank of Portugal has room to cut rates, but there is no urgency. I think it will wait to see what the Bank of Spain does," he said.
Martim Amaral Neto of Banco Essi said: "There are two reasons not to expect a rate cut -- inflation and the recent weakness of the escudo. The first factor is more important."
In January consumer prices rose 0.3 percent to give a year-on-year rate of 3.3 percent and an average annual rate of 3.2 percent.
